question.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ 7 \\ 5\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u\,⊥\,v.$ Find $(u-2v)\cdot (v+2w).$
question.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $u\cdot v=0.$ Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(u-2v)\cdot (v+2w) & =u\cdot v-2(v\cdot v)+2(u\cdot w)-4(v\cdot w) \\  & =0-2(v\cdot v)+2(u\cdot w)-4(v\cdot w) \\  & =-2(3\cdot 3+2\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-2)+2\cdot 2) \\  & +2((-2)\cdot 0+5\cdot 2+7\cdot 0+5\cdot (-3)) \\  & -4(3\cdot 0+2\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot 0+2\cdot (-3)) \\  & =-2(21)+2(-5)-4(-2) \\  & =-42-10+8 \\  & =-44.\end{aligned}
$$
